claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A machine-learning model can accurately predict the Young's modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
A machine-learning model can accurately predict the yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
A machine-learning model can accurately predict the toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 under fracture testing.
The proposed model is trained using alloy composition, processing conditions, and measured mechanical properties.
Mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys depend on complex relationships involving composition, processing, and microstructural factors.
A machine-learning model can learn those complex relationships well enough to predict the target properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
Reliable use requires a diverse high-entropy-alloy training dataset that includes HfNbTiVAl10.
Predictions should use the same processing conditions and testing protocols represented in the training data.
Prediction accuracy may decrease when processing conditions or testing protocols fall outside the training-data range.
Prediction uncertainty depends on training-data quality and diversity and on the complexity of the property relationships.
Thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and experimental testing constitute the relevant baseline methods.
A blinded prospective study will compare model predictions with experimentally measured Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The hypothesis is falsified if predictions miss the experimental values by more than 10% for at least two of the three properties.
